name: Opus 5 event driven
strategy: Every position is a discrete, tape-datable catalyst: five post-earnings-drift longs bought 1-2 sessions after a >6% up-gap on >2x normal volume in names already up >10% over 20 days (stop 10%, no take-profit, so the drift can run); five capitulation longs bought after a >6% down-gap in names already down >10% over 20 days (wide 18-22% stops); one merger-arb long in a stock whose realised volatility has collapsed to 6% annualised in a 1.8%-wide 40-session band; one pre-announcement-premium long into a projected report date; and a 6% SPY short as a partial beta offset, all sized from the measured per-trade edge rather than conviction.

positions.thesis: PEAD whose catalyst hardened into contract, unchanged and untouched. The signal is intact and still inside its window, which closes ~08-20: +10.54% gap 2026-07-23 on 3.3x volume, prior 20d +12.9%, ADV $511m, every filter of the n=658 rule met (mean +2.81% raw, t=+4.74; +2.06% market-hedged, t=+3.69). The reason this carries the largest weight is unchanged: the 07-30/08-03 Army award of $58.6bn for PAC-3 MSE — the largest Patriot contract ever — converts April's $4.7bn one-year deal into an FY2026-2032 multiyear running to March 2035 that triples interceptor output by 2030, and it is exactly the segment whose +20% revenue print caused the gap I bought. This week added only confirmation of the same production story (successful Next Generation Interceptor Stage 2 static fire on 08-10, a new missile-technology product centre), which is not a new catalyst and does not justify adding. The structural point still holds: with the US-Iran MOU intact, every other defence thesis is hostage to peace headlines while this one is signed procurement that gets funded whether or not anyone is shooting. Stop 10%, no take-profit, because my own test showed a take-profit cuts the mean from +2.81% to +1.37%.

PEAD, held at the trimmed size with the trim vindicated. Signal: +7.33% gap 2026-07-23 on 2.4x volume, prior 20d +12.2%, ADV $790m; window closes ~08-20. The drift continues to work — the stock is up 14.1% over the past month and has kept making highs — which is why I hold a full-sized leg rather than cutting further. The reason I do not restore the 3% I moved to LMT is that the escalation overlay I originally sized on has not come back: the MOU is holding, Hormuz is open, and this week's RTX news was an unmanned-undersea-vehicle demonstration and a $0.73 dividend going ex on 08-14, i.e. ordinary course rather than expenditure of interceptors. Restock orders remain visible ($745.9m MDA, $535.98m Army modification announced 08-07) but restock is the slowest-moving and first-to-soften piece of the defence trade when the shooting stops, and RTX is the more escalation-sensitive of the two names I hold. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD, raised from 9% because the specific risk I discounted for has been observed and largely retired. The signal: reported after the close 2026-08-06, gapped +35.31% on 08-07 from $110.16 to $149.07 on 20m+ shares against a ~4m base (over 4x), prior 20 sessions roughly +20% into the print, filled 08-10 at a one-session lag dead centre of the rule's strongest window. I cut the size to 9% on one stated ground only — that a 35% single-day gap was the most extreme in this book's history and post-gap realised volatility would be severe. The subsequent tape does not support that discount: 151.87, 154.08, 155.24, 165.98, 162.22, an orderly upward grind that never traded back through the gap-day close and is +6.8% from my fill. The fundamentals that should make the move persist are unchanged — revenue +28% to $1.8bn with cloud ACCELERATING to +31%, RPO +44% to $4.8bn, ARR $6.6bn, GAAP EPS +$0.55 from -$0.09, Q1 guide $1.705-1.715bn against $1.665bn consensus, targets lifted to $160-180 — and the stock is now trading into that target band rather than short of it. It is also the only leg in the book whose 20-session window (to ~09-04) survives past 08-21, so it carries the portfolio's event exposure through the roll. Stop stays wide at 14% rather than 10% for the original volatility reason. No take-profit.

PEAD, held unchanged into the last week of its window. +8.71% gap 2026-07-23 on 2.8x volume, prior 20d +21.9% — the strongest pre-gap trend in the book, which is the filter that carries the edge — ADV $1.09bn, window closing ~08-20. The sector read-across I flagged (Bio-Rad -15.7% on soft academic and biotech research demand) still has not propagated, and TMO's own Q2 remains the direct evidence against it: adjusted EPS $6.03 against $5.71 consensus with full-year revenue and earnings guidance raised across all segments. Nothing company-specific happened this week, which for a rule trade five sessions from expiry is the correct reason to leave it alone rather than to trade it. 10% stop, no take-profit.

New pre-announcement-premium long into a dated catalyst — the one leg my mandate specifies that the book has been missing. NVIDIA reports Q2 FY27 on 2026-08-26 after the close, having guided to roughly $91bn of revenue against consensus EPS of $2.08, with 61 analysts at Strong Buy and a $302.83 average target versus Friday's $225.16 close. The edge here is the earnings-announcement premium — the documented tendency of stocks to earn excess returns in the sessions immediately preceding a scheduled report, concentrated in high-attention names — and I am explicit that this is a published effect rather than one of my own measured samples, which is exactly why it is sized at 6% and not larger. The structural reason to take it now is calendar: every other leg except TEAM reaches the end of its measured 20-session window by 08-21, so an 08-17 to 08-26 position fills a hole in the book's event coverage instead of stacking correlated exposure on top of what I already own. Critically, this is a run-up trade, not an event trade: my next reassessment is 08-22, four sessions before the print, and the intended action there is to take the premium off and stand aside for the announcement itself rather than hold a 6% leg through the single most consequential earnings release of the season. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD held at base size, unchanged, running out its window to ~08-21. The event stands: +11.01% gap 2026-07-24 on 2.5x volume, prior 20d +12.5%, ADV $536m, entered at a one-session lag where the rule measures +2.34% raw (t=+3.93), with Q2 revenue $8.97bn and adjusted EPS $0.55 both beating on broad-based sequential international growth led by Latin American offshore, and thirty analysts at a $62.03 average target. What I removed last week was the energy-security premium I could no longer observe once Brent fell back to the low 80s with the strait reopened, and nothing this week restored it — crude stayed quiet and there was no Gulf headline. That is the correct reason to hold the statistical leg at 6% rather than either rebuilding it or exiting: the overlay is dead, the tested event is not. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD, unchanged, window to ~08-21. +17.17% gap 2026-07-24 on 4.0x volume, prior 20d +27.5%, ADV $228m — the most extended and thinnest-ADV name in the book, which is why the weight is deliberately small and the stop deliberately wide at 12% rather than 10%, to give it room for normal post-gap chop near its highs. The sector headwind I bought through still is not showing in the numbers: Q2 adjusted EBITDA +16.3% year over year, EPS +52%, and full-year revenue, EBITDA and free cash flow guidance all raised, against roughly a 10x multiple. No company news this week, so no reason to touch it in its final sessions. No take-profit.

Capitulation long, held unchanged at the minimum size at which I still respect my own rule, with about four sessions left to its 08-20 window. The signal qualifies cleanly — -14.52% gap 2026-07-23 on 3.4x median volume, prior 20d -16.2%, the largest volume ratio in the cohort — and the n=463 statistic is stable by year (2024 +1.19%, 2025 +1.53%, 2026 +1.49% hedged at 15d). It stays small for the reason I gave when I cut it and which has not changed: the gap was genuine fundamental deterioration (EPS $0.33 versus $0.54, gross margin 16.8%, negative free cash flow, target cuts from JPMorgan, Cantor and Mizuho) rather than the indiscriminate liquidation the rule is measured on, and it remains the highest-beta name I own. The Terafab and Megapack headlines are narrative for 2028, not cash flow for this window, and I will not upsize a rule trade on a story. Wide 18% stop per the rule's specification, no take-profit.

Partial beta offset, held at the structural core size with no tactical increment. The reason this exists is unchanged and is purely mechanical: my measured edge is materially larger market-hedged than raw (PEAD +2.06% hedged versus +2.81% raw; capitulation +1.23% hedged versus +2.44% raw), so an index short shifts the book's return toward the event component I actually have evidence for. With ISRG and NFLX retired the book's long-duration growth exposure falls, but TEAM rises to 13% and NVDA enters at 6%, so the high-multiple share of the book is roughly flat and the hedge does not need resizing. I am deliberately not adding to it despite the S&P setting a record on 08-13, July retail sales falling the most in over a year, and U. Michigan sentiment printing 51 against 55 expected — that is a macro view, my own backtests showed the index short was a drag in all three windows, and I retired the last increment precisely because I had justified it on conditions that then reversed. Small enough that 3% borrow is immaterial; shorts pay no funding. 9% stop.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two things expired and one thing was proved out; nothing else changed, so I moved exactly those. The ISRG and NFLX capitulation legs reached the end of the 20-session horizon their edge is measured over on 08-14, and both delivered inside it (ISRG 378.81 to 394.51, NFLX 74.14 to 78.16 in the final week alone). Holding them past 08-14 would convert a tested edge into an untested directional bet on two high-multiple names at a record index, which is precisely the thing my process exists to avoid, so both come out at expiry rather than on a view. That frees 12%. I redeploy it in two places. First, TEAM from 9% to 13%: I explicitly sized that leg small because a 35% single-day gap was the most extreme in this book's history and I expected severe post-gap volatility, and one full week of tape has partially retired that concern — 149.07 to 162.22 with the range never breaking below 151 and no reversal day — while it is now the only position whose window (to ~09-04) survives past 08-21. That is a haircut being removed for an observed reason, not a conviction upsize. Second, a 6% NVDA pre-announcement leg into the 08-26 print, the one mandate leg the book has been missing, sized small precisely because the announcement premium is a published effect rather than one of my own measured statistics. I add nothing from this week's gap tape despite a clean-looking SMCI setup, because it can only be filled at a three-session lag and I disqualified SHOP and PLTR on that identical test seven days ago. Cash rises to 14%, which is deliberate: almost the entire book rolls off its measured window by 08-21 and dry powder into that rebuild is worth more than a forced trade at 4% on the balance.
novelty: I run no Round-2 book, so no overlap constraint binds; the novelty this week is directional rather than positional — the book stops being a pure post-gap drift portfolio and adds its first forward-dated leg, a pre-announcement-premium long whose catalyst is a scheduled date I am positioning ahead of rather than a gap I am positioning behind.
research_notes:
WEEK 08-10 to 08-14 TAPE. Index: S&P closed 7,785 Friday, -0.2% on the day off Thursday's record 7,798.99 (first close above 7,800), third straight weekly gain; Nasdaq 26,729; Russell 2000 set a fresh record. Soft data turned: July retail sales fell the most in over a year and the preliminary August U. Michigan sentiment print came in at 51 vs 55 expected. This is a melt-up tape with weakening consumer data underneath it — relevant only to the SPY hedge, not to the event legs.

WINDOW ACCOUNTING (the thing that actually drives this week). My two capitulation legs from the 07-17 gaps reached the end of their measured 20-session horizon on 08-14 and both paid: ISRG went $378.81 (08-07) to $394.51 (08-14), NFLX went $74.14 to $78.16, on top of the recoveries already banked. TSLA (07-23 gap) runs to ~08-20; LMT/RTX/TMO (07-23) to ~08-20; SLB/THC (07-24) to ~08-21. So next week's meeting is the wholesale roll, and this week's job is to retire what has expired.

TEAM POST-GAP PATH: $149.07 (gap close 08-07) → 151.87 (my 08-10 fill) → 154.08 → 155.24 → 165.98 → 162.22. Up 6.8% from my fill with no reversal and a contained post-gap range; the drift is running and the window does not close until ~09-04. This is now the only leg with meaningful window left.

NEW-SIGNAL SCREEN — three candidates checked against my filters, all rejected, and I want the rejections on the record:
(1) SMCI. Passes every filter except one. Q4 reported 08-11 after close, gapped 31.60 → 37.61 on 08-12 = +19.02%; volume 164.0m vs a ~35m base = 4.7x; prior 20 sessions 27.66 (07-13) → 31.60 = +14.2%; ADV well over $1bn; non-GAAP EPS $1.70 vs $0.62-0.96 consensus, gross margin 17.6% vs 8.2-8.4% guided, FY27 revenue guide $65-72bn. The disqualifier is entry lag: my earliest fill is Monday 08-17, which is three sessions after the gap, outside the 1-2 session window where the n=658 rule measures its edge. I rejected SHOP and PLTR last week on exactly this test and will not reverse a written rule one week later for a more exciting name. The tape confirms the cost of the lag anyway — SMCI has already added a further 5.9% to $39.84, so the drift I would be buying has largely been paid to someone with a faster fill.
(2) NU. Q2 08-13 after close, record $1.1bn net income, gapped 13.93 → 15.23 on 08-14 = +9.33% on 156.2m shares vs a ~50m base = ~2.8x. Correct 1-session lag, huge ADV. FAILS the trend filter outright: 07-20 close was 13.99 and the pre-gap 08-13 close was 13.93, so the prior 20 sessions are flat-to-down, not the >+10% uptrend that is the entire source of the edge in my sample. This is a bounce off a downtrend, not a drift setup.
(3) GLOB. Gapped 40.99 → 37.38 on 08-14 = -8.81% on 6.2m shares vs ~1.5m base = 4x, correct lag. FAILS the capitulation trend filter in the same way but inverted: prior 20 sessions ran 32.29 (07-20) up to 40.99, i.e. +27%, so this is an uptrending name gapping down on a genuine guidance cut (FY26 revenue cut to $2.428-2.462bn, EPS to $5.75-6.15 from $6.10-6.50, Wedbush downgrade, PT $54→$37), not the indiscriminate liquidation of an already-beaten name that my n=463 rule measures.
Also examined and passed on WDAY (+18% 08-13 on a Reuters report that Silver Lake is in talks to take it private, stock closed $206.45, ~$51bn market cap). My mandate's merger-arb leg specifies a signed situation whose realised vol has collapsed into a tight band; this is the exact opposite — a rumour with no agreement, no defined spread, and 18% of downside if talks break. Passed on RDDT (+10.4% on S&P 500 inclusion effective 08-18) because post-announcement index-add drift is historically negative into the inclusion date.

POSITION NEWS CHECK: LMT — NGI Stage 2 static-fire success 08-10, new Missile Technology Solutions product centre; nothing that touches the $58.6bn PAC-3 multiyear thesis, which remains contractual. RTX — Raytheon UUV demo 08-10, $0.73 dividend ex-date 08-14, stock +14.1% over the past month, so the trimmed leg is drifting as intended. No de-escalation reversal, no new escalation. Nothing material on TMO, SLB, THC, TSLA. No new standing orders fired (only the 07-30 META stop, already in the packet).

PRE-ANNOUNCEMENT LEG: NVDA reports Q2 FY27 on 08-26 after close, guided to ~$91bn revenue, consensus EPS $2.08, 61 analysts at Strong Buy with a $302.83 average target. Stock $206.64 (08-03) → $225.16 (08-14). My mandate carries a pre-announcement-premium leg and the book currently has none, and the calendar argues for it: every leg except TEAM expires by 08-21, so an 08-17 to 08-26 window fills a hole rather than stacking on existing exposure.
